summary: Both halves inspected with magnification. Section120 is dated28.9 and generalizes binomial/divided-power operations through an analyzer. The long opening hand insertion is anchored after Yesterday, without a following comma. Three marginal instructions are circled: n at least minus one, à la ligne, and id. Several indexing corrections and the replacement yield a Omega-structure are clearly hand; extra, ing, and over k_0 within the tensor-power insertion are typed. The overwritten digits and a short cancelled word remain unresolved.

edits.reason: The pen insertion bracket descends immediately after Yesterday; move the insertion to its visible anchor, preserving the lack of a comma after it.
The unwanted typed n after with remains identifiable beneath its strike.
The cancelled word structural is recoverable under the replacement extra and the typewriter strikes.
The live minus one is certain, also repeated in the margin; the blackened earlier digit cannot be established as 1, so add explicit doubt.
The cancellation after act appears to preserve ion, making an earlier action, rather than ing; the heavy overstrikes still require doubt.
The live n is a serif typewriter overprint with another impression below it, rather than a hand letter. The previous impression remains uncertain.
The right-edge pen tail after finite type is visible as a comma on the lower-half image.
Within the insertion the Omega is hand-filled, but n and over k_0 have typewriter forms; preserve the mixed provenance.
The marginal correction is enclosed by a hand-drawn circle.
The instruction à la ligne is visibly enclosed by an oval; retain the author's actual instruction, not an editorial paraphrase.
The id instruction is likewise circled in the lower left margin.
